item.title: The Ripple Effect of Going for It
item.description: Can you learn to captain a yacht at 62 and turn it into a world-traveling lifestyle? Absolutely! Below, Sine Maria shares a first-hand account of her family’s latest charter with Dream Yacht in the Balearic Islands. Read on for an inspiring look at courage, partnership, and what happens when you say yes to a new adventure on the water. The Ripple Effect of Going for It On breaking into worlds you weren’t born into, and what happens when you actually do the thing. By: Good Life Designed and Sine Maria If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my mom, it’s that life has so much to offer and the limit of your world is only limited by your ability to keep expanding. In the middle of the pandemic, as part of our collective pause, she and I decided to go through the whole Good Life Designed program together again. It was through that process that she decided she wanted to be closer to nature, swim more, and learn how to sail. She didn’t grow up around sailing, knew it was costly and a bit of a boys club, but always admired the access it gave those who knew how. That hobby could take you anywhere in the world. The world of sailing requires a unique blend of resources, courage, technical education, practice, and willing crew members to go along for the ride and be there while you figure things out on your first trips alone. It thrives behind heavy yacht club doors that some are born with access into – but most don’t even know exist. The dream of being certified as a sailor has an even smaller niche- attracting those who thrive on the pressure to read and respond to the chaos of the elements at sea while holding the responsibility of passengers’ lives in their hands. Now that I have experienced the reward that comes with that kind of responsibility – I see the draw. Breaking Into a World You Weren’t Born Into I tried to look into data about women certified sailors but couldn’t find any credible data because no one seems to be particularly interested in that stat – however I can tell you there aren’t many. Sailing, just due to the nature of it, the time it requires, the unease that comes with the experience, especially as you’re getting your first solo trips under your belt, is enough to send anyone right over the edge. It’s heady, it’s overwhelming, it’s complicated, it’s technical, and it feels uncertain and dangerous before you’re skilled and experienced enough to feel truly comfortable and at ease on the water. When Pernille got the ping to learn to sail, the biggest question was how, as a 62-year-old woman, was she going to do it. She tried visiting yacht clubs but as someone who wasn’t interested in the social component and was really looking for the technical skills to captain her own ship, it didn’t feel like the best place to spend her time or money. The classes and day sail opportunities to get out on the water were nice, but if she really wanted to learn everything she needed to, she needed something different. She came across Nautilus Sailing, a week-long course in the Sea of Cortez that would teach you everything you need to know about sailing and cap off the week with a test that would certify you to sail on your own anywhere in the world. My dad at the time was in the most stressful period of his career, navigating his independent school and their 400 families through Covid. Using his coveted spring break to learn to navigate another set of uncharted territories felt not quite like the vacation he needed. But he took a leap of his own and joined her anyway. They spent a week disconnected from everything to focus on learning the thing that would later give them access to the life they live now – barely imaginable to them then. Heading out on what feel like once-in-a-lifetime week long sailing experiences all over the world with friends and family. item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. item.title: Sailing Strong: Chartering a Yacht in the Grenadines After Hurricane Beryl
item.description: In July 2024, Hurricane Beryl, a Category 4 storm, struck the Caribbean with unprecedented force, leaving a trail of devastation across Grenada and its neighboring islands. Particularly hard-hit were Carriacou and Petite Martinique, while the northern parts of the Grenadians sustained minimal damage. Despite the challenges, Grenada’s tourism infrastructure has made an impressive comeback, with many beloved destinations now open and ready to welcome travelers once again. This remarkable turnaround highlights the strength, beauty, and resilience of the island community. A Swift and Impressive Recovery The impact of Hurricane Beryl was severe, but ongoing restoration efforts have yielded tremendous progress. Popular islands and tourist hotspots have reopened marinas, restaurants, and resorts. Dream Yacht is fully operational with a well-maintained fleet ready for your sailing adventures. Our skilled staff is dedicated to delivering exceptional service, ensuring each charter provides a safe, comfortable, and unforgettable experience for those eager to explore the Grenadines. What Has Returned Post Hurricane? Bequia The island has been successfully restored, with no apparent traces of hurricane damage. Both the community and businesses are thriving here, with pristine beaches and vibrant lush forests. Bequia’s charm is untouched, a testament to the island’s dedicated restoration efforts, making it a delightful place to visit once again. Tobago Cays As always, the Tobago Cays remain a stunning sight. The crystal-clear waters and abundant marine life make them an ideal destination for snorkeling or simply unwinding by the shore. Numerous turtles still frequent this location and the coral reefs are in excellent condition. The famous Romeo’s, where the dishes are exceptionally fresh and flavorful, is as strong as ever. Although Petit Tabac is still in the process of recovery and not yet at its former glory, the recent replanting of palm trees signals a promising return. Meanwhile, Mr. Wonderful continues to delight visitors with his freshly baked bread, local fish, and his renowned banana bread – a true island treat. Union Island Union Island is the most impacted location along your charter route. Despite the damage, establishments like Carlos Bar are open and welcoming guests. The customs and immigration office are fully functional, and several grocery stores, as well as the popular fresh fish market, are operating. As an excellent alternative to stopping at Union Island, consider visiting Canouan instead. Canouan Canouan is back to normal post hurricane and ready for tourists. Sandy Lane Marina, is a recently built and fully operational resort in Canouan. It is a great place to unwind after a long day of sailing. The marina boasts first-rate facilities and provides a peaceful, secure docking spot and an incredible restaurant on site. Sandy Lane continues to impress by going above and beyond for visitors, featuring amenities like Randy’s well-stocked supermarket, where you can find nearly everything you need. Mayreau The iconic Saltwhistle Bay in Mayreau has fully returned to its vibrant atmosphere. A brand-new breakwater has been built to replace the one destroyed by Hurricane Beryl, significantly enhancing the bay’s charm and protection. The beach bars and restaurants bustling once again, including the famous Last Bar Before the Jungle. You will also find the mini-mart fully stocked and open. Visitors can enjoy the lively social scene, stunning scenery, and refreshing island vibes that make this bay a beloved destination in the Grenadines. Discover Charter Options from Grenada and Martinique Whether you’re an experienced sailor or simply looking to relax and enjoy the ride, we offer a variety of charter experiences to match your dream vacation.
